{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793012825045,"sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","part":{"id":"prt_177e4416f001Ipq2YIyt84V57a","messageID":"msg_177e43d87001wnrU9QNzvOuBsG","sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm checking the available GPU tools and compiler setup, and considering what \"equivalent semantics\" means here—likely requiring bitwise-identical results, which means I need to preserve the exact floating-point summation order from the original force computation loop.\n\nParallelizing over bodies i keeps each per-i sum order intact for bitwise equality, whether splitting across MPI ranks by block or across GPU threads, though FMA contraction differences between GCC's -march=native and nvcc's default fused multiply-add could still break exact matching between CPU and GPU. I should check output.txt to see if it holds a reference result I need to match.\n\nFor MPI, I'm planning a block-partition where each rank computes forces only for its own bodies against the full position array, updates velocity and position locally, then allgathers positions across ranks—this should produce results equivalent to the sequential version since initialization via randomizeBodies is deterministic and cheap enough to repeat on every rank.\n\nFor the final results, I'll gather the complete velocity array to rank 0 at the end, since positions are already synchronized across all ranks after the last allgather. I'll keep the overall timing and barrier structure from the original, then layer OpenMP parallelism over the per-rank body loop for both force computation and integration, and plan a CUDA kernel where each thread handles one body's force accumulation across all others for GPU acceleration.\n\nSince the task mandates unconditionally combining MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA with no CPU fallback, I'm deciding each MPI rank drives its own GPU (assigned via local rank mod device count), with CUDA kernels handling the force computation per rank's local bodies, and OpenMP covering host-side work like integration and reductions.\n\nI'm now worried about bitwise exactness: the original CPU version likely relies on GCC's default fast floating-point contraction with -march=native, folding operations into FMAs, which won't match GPU results from nvcc unless I account for that difference carefully — possibly keeping energy computation serial to avoid reduction-order discrepancies.\n\nWith both division and sqrt being IEEE correctly-rounded on GPU and CPU, and fmad/contraction disabled on both sides, the arithmetic should in principle line up bit-for-bit — though I still need to check whether the reference hash from the original build actually confirms that.\n\nLooking at the summation order per thread, the sequential dependency for Fx keeps the same order as the original, which helps. My plan is to disable FMA contraction uniformly across both the GPU device code and the host integration code, so that pos += vel*DT and similar operations match whatever the original build used, keeping everything consistent rather than trying to selectively enable fusion in just one place.\n\n","time":{"start":1793012810095,"end":1793012824985},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793012982113,"sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_017RKAsFLpHdgiDi3VgU3zaT","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/nbody/nbody.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA N-body benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI:    bodies are block-partitioned across ranks. Each rank owns the\n//             velocities and positions of its block and, after every step,\n//             the position blocks are exchanged with MPI_Allgatherv.\n//   - CUDA:   each rank drives one GPU (local rank mod visible device count).\n//             Force evaluation (shared-memory tiled O(N^2/P) per rank) and the\n//             position integration run on the device.\n//   - OpenMP: parallelizes the O(N^2) potential-energy evaluation used by the\n//             validation path on the root rank.\n//\n// Semantics: for every body i the sum over j is accumulated in the same order\n// as the original serial code, and the floating-point expressions are written\n// with explicit fma() where the original (GCC, -march=native) contracted them,\n// so results are independent of the number of ranks/GPUs and match the\n// original serial implementation.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr double SOFTENING = 1e-9;\nconstexpr double DT = 0.01;\nconstexpr int BLOCK = 256;  // threads per block; also the shared-memory tile size\n\nstruct Vec3 {\n    double x, y, z;\n    constexpr Vec3(const double x = 0, const double y = 0, const double z = 0) noexcept : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n};\nstatic_assert(sizeof(Vec3) == 3 * sizeof(double), \"Vec3 must be tightly packed for MPI transfers\");\n\nstruct Body {\n    Vec3 pos;\n    Vec3 vel;\n};\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                       \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,             \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                           \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\nvoid randomizeBodies(std::vector<Body>& bodies, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    for (auto& body : bodies) {\n        body.pos.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Force accumulation for the local bodies [0, nLocal) (global indices offset..).\n// Each thread owns one body and visits all n bodies in increasing j order, so\n// the per-body summation order equals the original serial loop. Tiles of\n// positions are staged in shared memory (SoA) to reuse loads across the block.\n__global__ void computeForcesKernel(const Vec3* __restrict__ pos, Vec3* __restrict__ vel,\n                                    const int n, const int offset, const int nLocal) {\n    __shared__ double sx[BLOCK], sy[BLOCK], sz[BLOCK];\n\n    const int li = blockIdx.x * BLOCK + threadIdx.x;\n    const bool active = li < nLocal;\n\n    double pix = 0.0, piy = 0.0, piz = 0.0;\n    if (active) {\n        pix = pos[offset + li].x;\n        piy = pos[offset + li].y;\n        piz = pos[offset + li].z;\n    }\n\n    double Fx = 0.0, Fy = 0.0, Fz = 0.0;\n\n    for (int base = 0; base < n; base += BLOCK) {\n        const int j = base + threadIdx.x;\n        if (j < n) {\n            sx[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].x;\n            sy[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].y;\n            sz[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].z;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const int cnt = (n - base < BLOCK) ? (n - base) : BLOCK;\n            for (int k = 0; k < cnt; ++k) {\n                const double dx = sx[k] - pix;\n                const double dy = sy[k] - piy;\n                const double dz = sz[k] - piz;\n                const double distSqr = fma(dz, dz, fma(dx, dx, dy * dy)) + SOFTENING;\n                const double invDist = 1.0 / sqrt(distSqr);\n                const double invDist3 = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n                Fx = fma(dx, invDist3, Fx);\n                Fy = fma(dy, invDist3, Fy);\n                Fz = fma(dz, invDist3, Fz);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        vel[li].x = fma(DT, Fx, vel[li].x);\n        vel[li].y = fma(DT, Fy, vel[li].y);\n        vel[li].z = fma(DT, Fz, vel[li].z);\n    }\n}\n\n// Position update for the local bodies. Must run after all force kernels have\n// finished (it is a separate launch, so stream ordering guarantees this).\n__global__ void integrateKernel(Vec3* __restrict__ pos, const Vec3* __restrict__ vel,\n                                const int offset, const int nLocal) {\n    const int li = blockIdx.x * BLOCK + threadIdx.x;\n    if (li < nLocal) {\n        const Vec3 v = vel[li];\n        Vec3& p = pos[offset + li];\n        p.x = fma(v.x, DT, p.x);\n        p.y = fma(v.y, DT, p.y);\n        p.z = fma(v.z, DT, p.z);\n    }\n}\n\n// Potential energy pair terms are computed in parallel (OpenMP) but accumulated\n// serially in the original order, so the result is bitwise identical.\ndouble computeTotalEnergy(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    double energy = 0.0;\n    const size_t n = bodies.size();\n\n    // Kinetic energy (assuming unit mass)\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        const double s = fma(body.vel.z, body.vel.z,\n                             fma(body.vel.x, body.vel.x, body.vel.y * body.vel.y));\n        energy = fma(0.5, s, energy);\n    }\n\n    // Potential energy (assuming unit mass for all bodies)\n    std::vector<double> term(n);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        const double xi = bodies[i].pos.x, yi = bodies[i].pos.y, zi = bodies[i].pos.z;\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n        for (long long jj = static_cast<long long>(i) + 1; jj < static_cast<long long>(n); ++jj) {\n            const size_t j = static_cast<size_t>(jj);\n            const double dx = bodies[j].pos.x - xi;\n            const double dy = bodies[j].pos.y - yi;\n            const double dz = bodies[j].pos.z - zi;\n            const double distSqr = fma(dz, dz, fma(dx, dx, dy * dy)) + SOFTENING;\n            term[j] = 1.0 / std::sqrt(distSqr);\n        }\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            energy -= term[j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    return energy;\n}\n\n// Validate that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\nbool validateSimulation(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        // Check for NaN or Inf values\n        if (!std::isfinite(body.pos.x) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.y) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.z) ||\n            !std::isfinite(body.vel.x) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.y) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.z)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value in body state\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Check for extreme values (bodies shouldn't fly off to infinity)\n        const double maxPos = 1e6;\n        const double maxVel = 1e6;\n        if (std::abs(body.pos.x) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.y) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.z) > maxPos) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body position exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (std::abs(body.vel.x) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.y) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.z) > maxVel) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body velocity exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of bodies (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Number of simulation steps       Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0, size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    int numBodies = 1024;\n    int numSteps = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank, so all ranks agree on exits)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numBodies = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numSteps = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (numBodies < 0) {\n        if (root) printf(\"Invalid number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"N-Body Simulation\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n        printf(\"Number of steps: %d\\n\", numSteps);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    const int N = numBodies;\n\n    // Bind this rank to a GPU: local rank (ranks sharing the node) mod device count.\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int deviceCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&deviceCount));\n    if (deviceCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Rank %d: no CUDA devices available\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(localRank % deviceCount));\n\n    // Block partition of bodies across ranks\n    std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n    {\n        const int base = N / size, rem = N % size;\n        int off = 0;\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            counts[r] = base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0);\n            displs[r] = off;\n            off += counts[r];\n        }\n    }\n    std::vector<int> countsD(size), displsD(size);  // in doubles (3 per body)\n    for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n        countsD[r] = 3 * counts[r];\n        displsD[r] = 3 * displs[r];\n    }\n    const int nLocal = counts[rank];\n    const int offset = static_cast<size_t>(N > 0 ? N : 1) * sizeof(Vec3);\n    const size_t localBytes = static_cast<size_t>(nLocal > 0 ? nLocal : 1) * sizeof(Vec3);\n\n    // Host staging buffer for the full position array (pinned for fast DMA)\n    Vec3* hPos = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&hPos), allBytes));\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) hPos[i] = bodies[i].pos;\n\n    Vec3 *dPos = nullptr, *dVel = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&dPos), allBytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void**>(&dVel), localBytes));\n    if (N > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPos, hPos, static_cast<size_t>(N) * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n    if (nLocal > 0) {\n        std::vector<Vec3> hVelLocal(nLocal);\n        for (int i = 0; cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n\n    const int gridLocal = (nLocal + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK;\n\n    // Run simulation\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = nLocal);\n            integrateKernel<<<gridLocal, BLOCK>>>(dPos, dVel, offset, nLocal);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n            // Local positions to host staging buffer\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(hPos + offset, dPos + offset,\n                                  static_cast<size_t>(nLocal) * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n\n        // Exchange position blocks so every rank has the full, updated state\n        MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, MPI_DATATYPE_NULL, hPos, countsD.data(), displsD.data(),\n                       MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        // Refresh remote position blocks on this rank's device (own block is already current)\n        if (offset > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPos, hPos, static_cast<size_t>(offset) * sizeof(Vec3),\n                                  cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n        }\n        const int tail = N - offset - nLocal;\n        if (tail > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPos + offset + nLocal, hPos + offset + nLocal,\n                                  static_cast<size_t>(tail) * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n        }\n    }\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    long long elapsedMs = duration.count(), maxMs = 0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&elapsedMs, &maxMs, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    if (root) printf(\"Simulation time: %lld ms\\n\", maxMs);\n\n    // Gather the full final state on the root when results or validation are requested\n    if (printResults || validate) {\n        std::vector<Vec3> hVelLocal(nLocal > 0 ? nLocal : 0);\n        if std::vector<Vec3> velAll(root ? static_cast<size_t>(N) : 0);\n        MPI_Gatherv(hVelLocal.data(), 3 * nLocal, MPI_DOUBLE,\n                    root ? reinterpret_cast<double*>(velAll.data()) : nullptr,\n                    countsD.data(), displsD.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        if (root) {\n            for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n                bodies[i].pos = bodyData.push_back(body.pos.x);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.pos.y);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.pos.z);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.x);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.y);\n            bodyData.push_back(body.vel.z);\n        }\n        print_results(bodyData, \"Bodies\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation: check that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\n    if (validate && root) {\n        printf(\"Validating simulation results...\\n\");\n\n        if (validateSimulation(bodies)) {\n            // Report final energy for architectures (override with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=...)\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 70 75 80 86 89 90)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The single translation unit contains both host code and CUDA kernels.\nset_source_files_properties(nbody.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\nadd_executable(nbody nbody.cpp)\n\n# Host code: optimized, no FP contraction beyond the explicit fma() calls, OpenMP enabled.\n# Device code: no implicit FMA contraction (explicit fma() only), IEEE sqrt/division.\ntarget_compile_options(nbody PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 --fmad=false\n        -Xcompiler=-O3,-march=native,-ffp-contract=off,-fopenmp,-Wall,-Wextra>)\ntarget_compile_options(nbody PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-Xcompiler=-fopenmp>)\ntarget_link_options(nbody PRIVATE {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793013440045,"sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","part":{"id":"prt_177ed4b89001nHMjbJIj2iDg0d","messageID":"msg_177ed47e2001iMOxvpPxFRIz1w","sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm seeing 60x speedup overall, but scaling from 1 to 4 GPUs shows no improvement at N=16384, which is suspicious — each rank should only handle a quarter of the work. I suspect all ranks might be binding to the same GPU despite the local rank assignment logic, possibly due to how MPI is configured with the run-as-root flag.\n\nChecking the math, np=1 achieves roughly 0.16 TFLOPS, which makes sense given FP64 div/sqrt operations are slow and latency-bound rather than throughput-bound. The real issue with np=4 is likely occupancy: splitting N=16384 across 4 GPUs leaves each with only 4096 threads, far below what's needed to saturate 82 SMs, so the kernel stays latency-bound instead of benefiting from parallelism — the fix would be to also parallelize the inner j-loop.\n\nBut doing a 2D decomposition over j would change the summation order and break the bitwise-equivalence requirement, so that's off the table given the exact-order constraint. Without reordering, parallelism is capped at one thread per body, meaning even np=1 only reaches about 10% occupancy; the remaining lever is improving instruction-level parallelism within each thread, since the sqrt/div for iteration k+1 is independent of the Fx accumulation chain and could overlap if the loop were unrolled.\n\nRunning the numbers on FP64 throughput — roughly 50 FP64 instructions per interaction across 2.7e9 interactions, against the 3090's limited FP64 lanes — predicts around 0.5s, close to the observed 0.33s, confirming np=1 is FP64-bound. But np=4 didn't scale because with only 4096 bodies per GPU, that's just 16 blocks spread across 82 SMs, so each GPU is massively underoccupied rather than compute-bound; the real bottleneck at np=4 is insufficient parallelism, not FP64 throughput. I need a way to increase blocks per GPU without altering the per-body summation order.\n\nThe issue is the sequential fma accumulation chain for forces can't be reordered without changing rounding, since each fma rounds the sum once including the exact product. I'm considering whether the expensive parts (sqrt/div for invDist3) could be precomputed in parallel ahead of the accumulation, though full N² storage is infeasible — maybe a tiled approach where a block precomputes values for a subset of j before the sequential reduction.\n\nI'm thinking through a tile-based design: threads compute distance and invDist3 values in parallel for (body, j) pairs into shared memory, then a smaller number of threads serially accumulate the forces per body across that tile. This splits the expensive per-pair math (parallel) from the cheap but order-dependent accumulation (serial), trying to balance tile size and thread count to maximize throughput while preserving the exact summation order per body.\n\nI'm also weighing whether this extra complexity is actually justified given the goal of max performance and scalability — multi-GPU scaling currently breaks down when the per-GPU body count drops too low relative to the fixed thread/block overhead.\n\nSo I'm sketching a concrete block design: 256 threads per block, 32 bodies per block, processing tiles of j-bodies at a time, with each thread computing several pairs and caching the dx/dy/dz/invDist3 terms in shared memory. I keep adjusting the tile size since the shared memory footprint grows fast — needing to shrink the tile from 64 down to 32 j's just to fit under the 48KB shared memory budget.\n\nNow I'm worried the serial accumulation phase per body will dominate runtime — the latency of looping over 32 shared-memory loads and fused multiply-adds per body could be much larger than the parallel pair computation itself, so I'm thinking about how to restructure the accumulation so the per-body loops run in parallel across threads rather than serially blocking the whole tile.\n\nGood, that matches the measured 33ms, so the accumulation chain isn't the bottleneck — throughput is. Now I'm questioning whether the expensive part really is sqrt/div at FP64 throughput on GA102.\n\nWorking it out: each pair needs roughly 30 FP64 ops once I account for the software sequences behind sqrt and div, giving about 8e10 total FP64 ops. GA102's FP64 throughput comes out to roughly 1.4–2.8e11 ops/s depending on how FMA is counted, so full-utilization time lands around 0.6s — which doesn't match what I'm seeing, so something else is going on.\n\nAt np=1 with N=16384, the measured 0.33s is roughly consistent with full-ish SM occupancy, but with only 64 blocks across 82 SMs and just 8 warps per block, latency hiding for FP64 is probably weak. Switching to a pairwise block design should help, so I'm sketching out an implementation: 32 bodies per block, 32 j-values per tile, 256 threads per block handling 4 pairs each, with shared memory arrays sized 1024 to hold the per-pair distance components and inverse-cube values, keeping the same accumulation order to preserve exactness.\n\nWriting the tile loop and shared-memory loading logic...\n\nStill writing kernel indexing...\n\nFor inactive bodies beyond nLocal, I'll just initialize their shared value to zero and skip pair computations for them, rather than letting uninitialized values compute harmlessly.\n\nWith 1024 pairs per tile and 32KB of shared memory storing 4 doubles per pair, I'm now worried about bank conflicts since threads with the same offset modulo 32 will hit the same bank 32-way when accessing the shared arrays.\n\nThe fix is to transpose the indexing so that for a fixed outer index, consecutive threads map to consecutive memory banks, making the access conflict-free. During accumulation only a fraction of threads stay active, which costs a bit of efficiency but keeps things correct, and for the grid sizing with nLocal=4096 I'm checking occupancy given the shared memory footprint per block across the available SMs.\n\nI'm considering alternate tile shapes (bodies-per-block vs j-bodies-per-tile) to balance shared memory use and sync count, planning to implement both and measure. Writing the kernel declaration with shared memory arrays for positions...\n\nStill writing kernel...\n\nConfirming dx uses the correct ordering, then syncing threads before applying the accumulated force to update each particle's velocity by DT times Fx.\n\nI need THREADS of 256 to comfortably exceed BI's 32 so accumulation threads exist, and I'm using BI as a power-of-two constant so the compiler can optimize the division into a shift. Pairs where ib+bi exceeds nLocal get skipped consistently in both computation and accumulation, and I'm tallying shared memory usage—roughly 8KB per 1024-double array, several arrays summing to about 32KB total.\n\nStatic shared memory stays under the 48KB limit, and the reciprocal square root for distance is computed once per pair by a single thread. I'm verifying the per-pair math matches the original formulation exactly—same dx/dy/dz differences, same fused-multiply-add chain for distSqr plus softening.\n\nNow I'm finalizing the kernel with BI and TJ defined as named constants with explanatory comments, then setting up the launch configuration with grid size based on ceiling division of nLocal by BI and block size equal to THREADS.\n\n","time":{"start":1793013402505,"end":1793013439935},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793013445351,"sessionID":"ses_e881bd88bffe47p93TSjawyriM","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_01JnxubeH63i26eqMroSW8pg","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/nbody/nbody.cpp","oldString":"// Force accumulation for the local bodies [0, nLocal) (global indices offset..).\n// Each thread owns one body and visits all n bodies in increasing j order, so\n// the per-body summation order equals the original serial loop. Tiles of\n// positions are staged in shared memory (SoA) to reuse loads across the block.\n__global__ void computeForcesKernel(const Vec3* __restrict__ pos, Vec3* __restrict__ vel,\n                                    const int n, const int offset, const int nLocal) {\n    __shared__ double sx[BLOCK], sy[BLOCK], sz[BLOCK];\n\n    const int li = blockIdx.x * BLOCK + threadIdx.x;\n    const bool active = li < nLocal;\n\n    double pix = 0.0, piy = 0.0, piz = 0.0;\n    if (active) {\n        pix = pos[offset + li].x;\n        piy = pos[offset + li].y;\n        piz = pos[offset + li].z;\n    }\n\n    double Fx = 0.0, Fy = 0.0, Fz = 0.0;\n\n    for (int base = 0; base < n; base += BLOCK) {\n        const int j = base + threadIdx.x;\n        if (j < n) {\n            sx[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].x;\n            sy[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].y;\n            sz[threadIdx.x] = pos[j].z;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const int cnt = (n - base < BLOCK) ? (n - base) : BLOCK;\n            for (int k = 0; k < cnt; ++k) {\n                const double dx = sx[k] - pix;\n                const double dy = sy[k] - piy;\n                const double dz = sz[k] - piz;\n                const double distSqr = fma(dz, dz, fma(dx, dx, dy * dy)) + SOFTENING;\n                const double invDist = 1.0 / sqrt(distSqr);\n                const double invDist3 = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n                Fx = fma(dx, invDist3, Fx);\n                Fy = fma(dy, invDist3, Fy);\n                Fz = fma(dz, invDist3, Fz);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        vel[li].x += DT * Fx;\n        vel[li].y += DT * Fy;\n        vel[li].z += DT * Fz;\n    }\n}","newString":"// Force accumulation for the local bodies [0, nLocal) (global indices offset..).\n//\n// Work decomposition inside a block: BI bodies x TJ source bodies per tile.\n//   1. All threads evaluate the pair terms (dx, dy, dz, 1/|r|^3) of the tile in\n//      parallel and stage them in shared memory.\n//   2. One thread per body accumulates its force by walking the tile's j in\n//      increasing order, carrying the accumulator across tiles.\n// Every body therefore sums its terms in exactly the order of the original\n// serial loop (j = 0..n-1), while the expensive sqrt/division work is spread\n// over the whole block, which keeps the GPU occupied even when a rank owns\n// only a few thousand bodies.\nconstexpr int BI = 32;       // bodies per block\nconstexpr int TJ = 32;       // source bodies per tile\nconstexpr int THREADS = 256; // threads per block (>= BI)\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(THREADS)\ncomputeForcesKernel(const Vec3* __restrict__ pos, Vec3* __restrict__ vel,\n                    const int n, const int offset, const int nLocal) {\n    __shared__ double siX[BI], siY[BI], siZ[BI];    // positions of this block's bodies\n    __shared__ double sjX[TJ], sjY[TJ], sjZ[TJ];    // positions of the current tile\n    __shared__ double pDx[BI * TJ], pDy[BI * TJ], pDz[BI * TJ], pInv3[BI * TJ];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ib = blockIdx.x * BI;               // first local body of this block\n    const bool accumThread = (tid < BI) && (ib + tid < nLocal);\n\n    if (tid < BI) {\n        const int li = ib + tid;\n        const bool valid = li < nLocal;\n        siX[tid] = valid ? pos[offset + li].x : 0.0;\n        siY[tid] = valid ? pos[offset + li].y : 0.0;\n        siZ[tid] = valid ? pos[offset + li].z : 0.0;\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    double Fx = 0.0, Fy = 0.0, Fz = 0.0;  // accumulators (used by threads tid < BI)\n\n    for (int base = 0; base < n; base += TJ) {\n        const int cnt = (n - base < TJ) ? (n - base) : TJ;\n\n        if (tid < cnt) {\n            sjX[tid] = pos[base + tid].x;\n            sjY[tid] = pos[base + tid].y;\n            sjZ[tid] = pos[base + tid].z;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        // Phase 1: pair terms. Layout p = bj * BI + bi keeps accumulation reads conflict-free.\n        for (int p = tid; p < cnt * BI; p += THREADS) {\n            const int bj = p / BI;\n            const int bi = p - bj * BI;\n            if (ib + bi < nLocal) {\n                const double dx = sjX[bj] - siX[bi];\n                const double dy = sjY[bj] - siY[bi];\n                const double dz = sjZ[bj] - siZ[bi];\n                const double distSqr = fma(dz, dz, fma(dx, dx, dy * dy)) + SOFTENING;\n                const double invDist = 1.0 / sqrt(distSqr);\n                pDx[p] = dx;\n                pDy[p] = dy;\n                pDz[p] = dz;\n                pInv3[p] = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        // Phase 2: ordered accumulation over the tile (ascending j)\n        if (accumThread) {\n            for (int bj = 0; bj < cnt; ++bj) {\n                const int p = bj * BI + tid;\n                Fx = fma(pDx[p], pInv3[p], Fx);\n                Fy = fma(pDy[p], pInv3[p], Fy);\n                Fz = fma(pDz[p], pInv3[p], Fz);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (accumThread) {\n        const int li = ib + tid;\n        vel[li].x += DT * Fx;\n        vel[li].y += DT * Fy;\n        vel[li].z += DT * Fz;\n    }\n}"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/nbody/nbody.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/nbody/nbody.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/nbody/nbody.cpp\n@@ -64,54 +64,86 @@\n     }\n }\n \n // Force accumulation for the local bodies [0, nLocal) (global indices offset..).\n-// Each thread owns one body and visits all n bodies in increasing j order, so\n-// the per-body summation order equals the original serial loop. Each rank owns the\n//             velocities and positions of its block and, after every step,\n//             the position blocks are exchanged with MPI_Allgatherv.\n//   - CUDA:   each rank drives one GPU (local rank mod visible device count).\n//             Force evaluation (shared-memory tiled O(N^2/P) per rank) and the\n//             position integration run on the device.\n//   - OpenMP: parallelizes the O(N^2) potential-energy evaluation used by the\n//             validation path on the root rank.\n//\n// Semantics: for every body i the sum over j is accumulated in the same order\n// as the original serial code, and the floating-point expressions are written\n// with explicit fma() where the original (GCC, -march=native) contracted them,\n// so results are independent of the number of ranks/GPUs and match the\n// original serial implementation.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr double SOFTENING = 1e-9;\nconstexpr double DT = 0.01;\nconstexpr int BLOCK = 256;
